Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C., Manoj Kumar Kushwaha (S.C.)
Hon'ble Arun Bhansali,Chief Justice
Hon'ble Vikas Budhwar,J.
1.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner aggrieved of the order dated 21.08.2024 passed by the District Magistrate, Agra under Section 72 of the U.P. Excise Act, 1910 ('the Act') whereby the petitioner has been called upon to produce F.D. to the tune of Rs.3,57,500/- and an undertaking pertaining to not dealing with the vehicle in question.
2. It is inter alia indicated in the petition that petitioner is registered owner of the vehicle No.
HR12AP4672 (Venue Car).

During patrolling/ checking the vehicle of the petitioner and one vehicle No. UP23AT3657 were stopped and searched wherein illegal liquor was found in the other vehicle, a recovery memo was prepared and case was registered as Case Crime No. 0925 of 2022, under Sections 60, 72 of the U.P. Excise Act and under Sections 420, 467, 468 and 471 IPC.
The vehicle of the petitioner was also seized.

3. On an application made by the petitioner, by order dated 31.03.2023, the Chief Judicial Manish vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4996857/
1 Magistrate, Agra, ordered for release of the vehicle based on the conditions indicated therein.

sentences.text: Whereafter the petitioner received notice under Section 72 issued on 15.05.2023, to which the reply was filed by the petitioner inter alia indicating that the vehicle in question was not used for carrying the illegal liquor and, therefore, the provisions of Section 72 would have no application.

However,
the District Magistrate, by the order impugned, ordered for depositing fixed deposit and an undertaking, as noticed hereinbefore.

4. Counsel for the petitioner made submissions, with reference to provisions of Section 72 of the Act that the vehicle can be confiscated only in a case where the same has been used for carrying illegal liquor and as admittedly, the vehicle of the petitioner was not being used for carrying any of the illegal liquor, the provision has no application and, therefore, the order impugned deserves to be quashed and set aside.
5.
Learned counsel for the respondents supported the order impugned.
Submissions have been made that petitioner is being prosecuted and challan has been filed against him and, therefore, the order passed is justified.
6. We have considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties and have perused the material available on record.

7. Provisions of Section 72 of the Act insofar as relevant reads as under:
"72. What things are liable to confiscation.

2 8.

entities.text: Manish vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the above provision would reveal that every conveyance used for carrying receptacles or package, reference whereof has been made in the previous sub-sections (a) to (d) shall be liable to confiscation.

Admittedly and from the perusal of the orders passed by the authority, it is apparent that the allegations against the petitioner was that he was doing the reiki while the illegal intoxicant was being carrying in the other vehicle.
There are no allegations that the illegal intoxicant was being transported/ carried in the vehicle of the petitioner.

In that view of the matter, the provisions of Section 72 (1)(e) of the Act, have no application to the case and consequently, the entire exercise by the respondents under Section 72 qua the petitioner's vehicle cannot be countenanced.
9. Consequently, the petition is allowed.
The order dated 21.08.2024 passed by the District Magistrate, Agra is quashed and set aside.
